subject: Brightline Order Form — clarifying output ownership & training carve-outs
messages:
From: Nathan Price <nathan.price@brightline.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightline.com, elena.marks@brightline.com
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form v2 (redlines) — training / output question

Kim / Vanessa,

Thanks for sending the updated Order Form. We circulated it to legal and procurement and have two narrow but material asks before we can sign:

1) Output ownership: Our legal team is requesting explicit language that output generated by Brightline data (customer prompts + proprietary data) is owned by Brightline, and that Redwood will not assert rights to customer outputs for any purpose other than to provide the service.
2) Training & feedback: Procurement wants a carve-out so Brightline data (including derived outputs) cannot be used to further train or tune Redwood models, either automatically or via a feedback license, unless Brightline opts in via a separate written agreement.

We attached our redlines to the Order Form (see Brightline_OrderForm_v2_redlines.pdf). We understand Redwood's platform benefits from feedback and telemetry, so we are open to a limited telemetry/ops data share for troubleshooting, but that should be expressly scoped and anonymized.

Can you confirm whether those two items are acceptable or propose language we can route to our GC? We want to avoid delaying the PO but need to get these clarified.

Thanks,
Nathan
Nathan Price
Head of Data Partnerships — Brightline
procurement@brightline.com

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com (Kimberly Park) <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Nathan Price <nathan.price@brightline.com>, Elena Marks <elena.marks@brightline.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form v2 (redlines) — training / output question

Nathan / Elena —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redlines. Looping in Vanessa (Commercial) and Connor (Legal Ops/Contracts) so we can align across product and legal. High-level response:

- Output ownership: Redwood's standard posture is to grant customers full rights to their outputs for their internal and commercial use; Redwood does not assert ownership in customer outputs. We are happy to incorporate explicit output title language in the Order Form that reflects Brightline's needs.

- Training & feedback: We can make a carve-out for customer-provided data and customer outputs such that they will not be used to train or improve Redwood models unless Brightline provides an explicit opt-in. However, operational telemetry (metrics, error traces) used purely for service stability can remain subject to an anonymized and aggregated usage clause; we will propose tight language.

Action items for us: Connor — can you draft specific clauses for the Order Form and a short MSA amendment language that we can send back to Brightline? Vanessa — I'll coordinate commercial concessions if they ask for a pricing credit tied to the carve-out.

Nathan — I'll follow up with a draft within 24 hours and flag any language points that require GC-to-GC discussion. If you prefer, we can do a quick 20-min call early next week to finalize.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

To: connor.obrien@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Mar 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: Brightline carve-out language options

Connor / Kim —

Quick internal note before we send the formal clause set to Brightline:

1) For customers asking that outputs are "owned" by them, the cleanest route is an express grant: Redwood confirms that customer outputs are the sole property of the customer and Redwood disclaims any ownership claims. That solves procurement's checkbox while keeping our telemetry safe.

2) For the training carve-out, propose two-tier language:
   - Opt-out by default: Customer data and outputs will NOT be used to train or improve Redwood models unless customer provides written opt-in.
   - Support/ops telemetry: Redwood may collect anonymized operational telemetry (latency metrics, crash traces, model id, prompt lengths) for service quality and debugging, explicitly excluding prompt and output content.

3) Commercial ask: Brightline may request a price uplift for opting into training (i.e., if they want to allow training for product improvements). If they demand free training prohibition, we should be prepared with a modest fee to offset lost model-improvement signal.

I can draft the email to Brightline once Connor provides the legal-safe clause.

-V
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | (650) 555-0149

Subject: Re: Order Form v2 (redlines) — training / output question

Kim, Vanessa, Connor —

Thanks for the quick engagement and proposed approach. The two-tier framing looks reasonable. A few quick points from our GC after reviewing your suggested carve-out:

- Please make sure the definition of "operational telemetry" is narrow and explicitly excludes any prompt or output content.
- We'll want a short amendment language for the Order Form that says: "Customer data and Customer Outputs shall not be used to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve Supplier's models without Customer's prior written consent."
- Brightline is open to a one-time commercial fee if Redwood requires it to maintain an opt-out. If you can provide an estimate range, that will speed procurement.

How fast can you send redline-ready text? We can aim to close next week if the language is clean.

Best,
Nathan
Head of Data Partnerships — Brightline
